about: UT-IGSP's own published measurements, one file per lane; the release summary's UT-IGSP entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for Andrey's fits; the reference's fits ran in an earlier job on the same data, which the build regenerated identically
comparator: graphical-model-learning 0.1a8 (unknown_target_igsp) with conditional-independence 0.1a6 and graphical-models 0.1a21, the authors' library and the method's only implementation

rows.J2: Andrey at its defaults against the reference at alpha 1e-5 and nruns 5 (the paper's level, the library's default runs and objective)
rows.J1: Andrey at alpha 1e-5 and 5 starts against the same reference fits

data: andrey.data: an Erdos-Renyi DAG on 20 variables with exactly 15 edges (mean degree 1.5), weights uniform on [0.25, 1] in absolute value with a random sign, standard normal noise (scale='raw'), columns in an order drawn from the seed; an observational environment and 5 settings of n rows each, each setting with one designed target, which the fit is told, and l off-targets, which it is not; out-of-claim cells change one of these as their fields say
fit_protocol: every package of a dataset in its own child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; 5 draws per dataset in claim (Andrey seed 0-4, the library's Python random and NumPy global generator seeded 0-4), one out of claim; a cap of 1,800 s per draw (3,600 s at 100 variables and with kernel tests), a timeout never scored
verdict_rule: per cell, row, and metric (shd, target_error): D = error(Andrey) - error(reference) per dataset, each the mean over 5 draws; side = where the 95% percentile bootstrap interval of mean D (10,000 resamples) lies; worse = above 0 on seeds 0-19 and on the rerun on seeds 2000-2019; better = below 0 on seeds 0-19 and on a second set (seeds 2000-2019, or for J2 the confirmation's seeds 4000-4019); a row with both is better when either lies below 0 (one row: J2 G2_perfect_l1_n1000 shd, below 0 on 2000-2019, contains 0 on 4000-4019); otherwise the row is named by its side on seeds 0-19 and 'not replicated', or 'tie'. Seeds 4000-4019 are the seeds on which J2's default was chosen, as the setting with the most rows below 0 there, so they favor below 0 for J2: 17 of J2's 18 better rows repeated there, 1 on seeds 2000-2019
residue_note: a side is read after rounding the interval's ends to 10 decimals: three ends are floating-point residue of an exact 0 (5e-18 and -6e-18 in the final rows J2 G1_shift_l3_n3000 shd and J1 G6_weight_l0_n1000 target_error, 2e-17 in the confirmation's a1e-05_lexicographic_s10 G2_perfect_l1_n1000 shd), so those intervals touch 0 and the rows tie; the run's own scripts read them as above or below 0, which changed no decision. The same reading moves the first of them from above 0 to contains 0 in default_selection.trace.inv_n_sum_counts. Counts of single runs name sides (below 0, contains 0, above 0); better and worse name only comparisons that repeated
error_metric: shd: pairs whose endpoint marks differ between the returned interventional essential graph, under the targets returned, and the true one; target_error: false plus missed targets over the settings

reference_at_andrey_level.what: the reference's UT-IGSP at Andrey's default level, alpha = 1 / observational rows for both tests and nruns = 10, against Andrey at its defaults (J2)

speed.note: Andrey's fits of the final build and the reused reference fits ran in separate jobs on the same processor model; the first campaign ran both back to back
speed.ratio: per dataset, Andrey's median fit time over its draws divided by the reference J1's, both on one pinned core with one BLAS thread
